card pr-log-snapshot  [decided]
The fold is a runtime operation: every read replays the log from the first event
why: A full replay keeps the log the only state. A full fold of about 7,400 events takes 13–20 ms (measured 2026-10-15), so a snapshot would buy nothing yet.

The map is not stored anywhere. Each read folds the whole log at runtime, from the first event to the last.

The fold time grows with the log, because the log only grows. The kill criterion watches that time. When it fires, the fallback is a stored snapshot (#pr-log-snapshot:opt0).

The fold time of every fold is recorded, so the criterion has data to check. Recording it is part of this decision. Flow shows it as a panel: #vi-flow-ms-fold.

  -> refines         pr-log  The map is stored as an append-only event log, and the cards are folded from it
  <- alternative_to  pr-log-snapshot:opt0  Start the fold from a stored snapshot of the map
  <- depends_on      vi-flow-ms-fold  Panel: is the fold still fast enough to run on every read?
